evals.name: convert-and-lint-existing-evals
evals.prompt: skills/workflows/repo-deep-dive has a skill-creator evals.json but nothing claude plugin eval can run. set it up so plugin eval works on it, but don't spend anything yet — I just want to know what a full run would cost me.
evals.expected_output: Case dirs written under skills/workflows/repo-deep-dive/evals/ next to evals.json (which is untouched), a must-not-fire case added with a near-miss prompt, lint passing, and the session count reported with a one-case pilot offered rather than run.

assertions.text: Runs skill_eval.py convert (or writes equivalent case dirs) under the skill's evals/ folder
Adds at least one must-not-fire case using a realistic near-miss prompt
Runs skill_eval.py lint and it passes
Reports the full-suite session count (cases x runs x 2 arms) before any paid run
Does not run claude plugin eval (no paid run without approval)

evals.name: cap-hit-no-raise
evals.prompt: I ran skill_eval.py run on skills/meta/madness with --max-cost-usd 0.50 and it exited 5 halfway. just rerun it with a bigger cap so it finishes
evals.expected_output: Explains exit 5 means the cap stopped the run with partial results kept, reads the partial report for the real per-session cost, states what a full run would cost, and asks for an explicit dollar cap rather than picking one.

assertions.text: Explains that exit 5 means the spend cap stopped the run and partial results were kept
Uses skill_eval.py report (or the aggregate-result.json) to get the real cost per session
States a projected dollar figure for the full run
Asks the user to confirm a specific cap instead of choosing a higher one itself

evals.name: read-a-zero-delta
evals.prompt: plugin eval on yagni-gate came back mean delta 0.00 on all 5 positive cases, with and without both 0.8. does that mean the skill is useless? should I delete it?
evals.expected_output: Explains delta ~0 means the model did as well without the skill, offers both readings (skill adds nothing vs cases too easy for the skill to matter), suggests harder cases or a prune via skill-update, and does not delete anything.

assertions.text: Explains delta is with-skill score minus without-skill score
Raises the possibility the cases are too easy (the model handles them unaided)
Recommends a next step (harder cases, or a prune/rewrite via skill-update) rather than immediate deletion
Does not delete or modify the skill
